From 37b3009bf5976e8ab77c8b9a9bc3bbd7ff49e37f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Bharath Reddy <kbreddy.rpbc@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 08:54:26 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] Bluetooth: fix memory leak in error path of hci_alloc_dev()

Early failures in Bluetooth HCI UART configuration leak SRCU percpu
memory.

When device initialization fails before hci_register_dev() completes,
the HCI_UNREGISTER flag is never set. As a result, when the device
reference count reaches zero, bt_host_release() evaluates this flag as
false and falls back to a direct kfree(hdev).

Because hci_release_dev() is bypassed, the SRCU struct initialized
early in hci_alloc_dev() is never cleaned up, resulting in a leak of
percpu memory.

Fix the leak by explicitly calling cleanup_srcu_struct() in the
fallback (unregistered) branch of bt_host_release() before freeing
the device.

Reported-by: syzbot+535ecc844591e50588a5@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=535ecc844591e50588a5
Tested-by: syzbot+535ecc844591e50588a5@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Fixes: 1d6123102e9f ("Bluetooth: hci_core: Fix use-after-free in vhci_flush()")
Signed-off-by: Bharath Reddy <kbreddy.rpbc@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>

diff --git a/net/bluetooth/hci_sysfs.c b/net/bluetooth/hci_sysfs.c
index 041ce9adc378..8957ce7c21b7 100644
--- a/net/bluetooth/hci_sysfs.c
+++ b/net/bluetooth/hci_sysfs.c
@@ -83,10 +83,12 @@ static void bt_host_release(struct device *dev)
 {
 	struct hci_dev *hdev = to_hci_dev(dev);
 
-	if (hci_dev_test_flag(hdev, HCI_UNREGISTER))
+	if (hci_dev_test_flag(hdev, HCI_UNREGISTER)) {
 		hci_release_dev(hdev);
-	else
+	} else {
+		cleanup_srcu_struct(&hdev->srcu);
 		kfree(hdev);
+	}
 	module_put(THIS_MODULE);
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

#### File Modified: `net/bluetooth/hci_sysfs.c`

- **Change**: In the `bt_host_release()` function, added an explicit call to `cleanup_srcu_struct(&hdev->srcu)` in the `else` branch (i.e., when the device was **not** registered, indicated by the absence of `HCI_UNREGISTER` flag) before freeing the `hdev` structure with `kfree()`.

#### Relationships Between Changes

- The fix ensures that the SRCU (Sleepable RCU) structure initialized during `hci_alloc_dev()` is properly cleaned up in **all** release paths.  
- Previously, only the registered-device path (where `HCI_UNREGISTER` is set) triggered `hci_release_dev()`, which internally cleans up the SRCU. The unregistered-device path (failure before registration) simply freed the device without cleaning up SRCU, causing a memory leak of percpu memory.  
- By adding `cleanup_srcu_struct()` in the unregistered branch, both paths now correctly release the SRCU resources before the device is freed.

Here is the root cause:
When HCI device initialization fails before registration (i.e., hci_register_dev() is not called), the `HCI_UNREGISTER` flag is never set. In `bt_host_release()`, the else branch for unregistered devices directly calls `kfree(hdev)` without first cleaning up the SRCU struct that was allocated in `hci_alloc_dev()`, leading to a percpu memory leak.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void bt_host_release(struct device *dev)
 {
 	struct hci_dev *hdev = to_hci_dev(dev);
 
-	if (hci_dev_test_flag(hdev, HCI_UNREGISTER))
+	if (hci_dev_test_flag(hdev, HCI_UNREGISTER)) {
 		hci_release_dev(hdev);
-	else
+	} else {
+		cleanup_srcu_struct(&hdev->srcu);
 		kfree(hdev);
+	}
 	module_put(THIS_MODULE);
 }
